title.narrative: Climate adaptation, mitigation, environment and biodiversity

description.narrative: DFAT, in partnership with The Asia Foundation, is advancing Women’s Climate Resilience (WCR) in Mongolia by strengthening the resilience and leadership of women facing climate-induced migration. ‍ WCR delivered tangible results through inclusive and locally grounded solutions. Nearly 1,000 women entrepreneurs across two locations were provided with training, mentorship sessions, and incubator programs enabling climate-aware business development and peer networks. ‍ Through pioneering a carbon credit incentive mechanism developed by a local start-up, seven ger households, including six women-led households, transitioned from coal to solar-powered heating systems. Results included a reduction in electricity costs and improvements in indoor air quality. Maintenance training, routine post-installation inspections, insulation and enhanced air ventilation were included in the project to ensure ongoing effectiveness and sustainability. ‍ Leadership development is also a key focus of the program. The Asia Women Leaders Program trained 24 government-affiliated mid-career women on climate and gender-responsive leadership, prompting an expansion of national commitment. Additionally, the forthcoming Women’s Leadership in Green Finance Fellowship within the program will further position women as drivers of inclusive and sustainable finance. ‍ WCR’s first year demonstrates a strong foundation for scale, innovation, and sustained impact aligned with the program’s strategic objectives.
